title: VPC multi-NIC boundary, offline bootstrap and operator compatibility PRD
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: Customers running Redwood Private in complex datacenter and VPC environments are asking for a clear contract that guarantees successful bootstrap, safe in-place and operator-driven upgrades, and well-defined network boundaries when multiple NICs, split-horizon DNS, or constrained egress policies exist. This PRD captures requirements, scope limitations, and acceptance criteria for multi-NIC topologies, offline/bootstrap media, and operator compatibility during upgrades. The goal is to define deterministic checks and operational playbooks so teams can certify private deployments (on-prem and isolated VPCs) without ad-hoc runbooks.
background: Observed failures in recent beta: (1) MTU mismatches between host NICs and overlay caused KV cache sync timeouts; (2) airgapped bootstrap using a mirror failed when manifest signature verification required a remote KMS; (3) operator in-place upgrades left a small percentage of nodes NotReady when a secondary NIC had no route to the image mirror. Customers require: predictable bootstrap with zero or limited egress, deterministic upgrade rollback, and a lightweight operator verification harness that runs pre- and post-upgrade probes.
scope: Define network contract for multi-NIC hosts (control plane vs data plane interfaces), including recommended routing and priority rules
Design and validate an offline bootstrap flow that supports signed artifact mirroring, physical-media ingestion, and time-limited egress allowlists
Define operator readiness and upgrade compatibility checks (preflight probes, MTU/DNS/egress checks, checksum validation)
Specify acceptance criteria and automated tests for canary and staged upgrades in constrained networks
out_of_scope: Full operator rework — we will add compatibility hooks and preflight checks but not rewrite the operator
Network hardware-specific drivers or vendor-level NIC firmware fixes
acceptance_criteria: Bootstrap: Fresh cluster can bootstrap to Ready state with zero external egress when provided a signed mirror tarball and operator manifest. Verification: end-to-end deployment test that exercises image pull and manifest signature validation using local KMS or offline signing key.

Image verification: All images are validated via a signed manifest (protobuf/JSON) and tolerated upgrade requires a manifest signature validated by the operator using a customer-provided public key. Failure mode: operator refuses to start if signature missing or invalid.

MTU/DNS: Operator preflight must detect MTU mismatches > 100 bytes between primary and secondary NICs and fail with clear remediation steps. Split-horizon DNS entries required for control-plane endpoints must be validated by a synthetic DNS resolver before proceeding with an upgrade.

Canary progression: Canary nodes (configurable N=2 by default) must run for a configurable observation window (default 15 minutes). Canary metrics (CPU, RPC error rate, token-latency, KV sync lag) must remain within the defined SLO deltas (no more than 10% regression) before proceeding to 25% rollout.

Operator rollback: If >5% nodes report NotReady after 10 minutes post-rollout step for the staged group, operator must automatically initiate a rollback to the prior image and mark the rollout as failed; rollback completion must bring cluster to the pre-rollout health baseline.

Egress allowlist window: For customers requiring temporary egress, operator must support a time-bound allowlist presigned by the control plane; the window must be auditable and revocable by the customer. Example: a 2-hour presigned mirror-access token recorded in audit logs.

Physical-media fallback: Operator supports a documented USB/ISO image ingestion pathway; ingestion must validate image checksums and signatures and produce the same readiness outcome as network-based mirroring within 30 minutes on a reference 5-node cluster.

Offline KMS rotation: KMS key rotation for offline deployments must be supported via an offline key-import procedure; rotation must complete without cluster downtime and be reversible within the operator (audit trail retained).

Operator readiness endpoints: Operator must expose preflight endpoints (/preflight/egress, /preflight/mtu, /preflight/dns, /preflight/signature) which return machine-readable results and human-readable remediation hints.

Telemetry gating: Upgrade controller may proceed only when ingestion of pre-upgrade metrics (sampling rate 1%) confirms telemetry channel health; if telemetry is degraded, operator enters a paused state and requires explicit user approval to continue.
success_metrics: Reduction in deployment support tickets related to networking/bootstrap failures by 70% for customers on the pilot program
95% of pilot private clusters able to complete a full staged upgrade with automatic rollback engaged when anomalies exceed thresholds
Automated preflight checks covering 90% of common failure modes seen in last 6 months incidents
risks: Operator complexity: Adding many preflight checks increases operator surface area and maintenance burden
Edge networking permutations: There may be untested vendor NIC behaviors (e.g., SR-IOV setups) that we do not catch in CI
Security posture: Supporting temporary egress or physical media introduces procedural risks—must enforce strict signing and auditing

ENG-22645: signed-manifest format and offline signing toolchain
ENG-23011: telemetry sampling & ingestion reliability improvements

notes: PM decision 2025-02-20: prioritize deterministic checks over best-effort heuristics; we will fail fast and provide clear remediation guidance.
Design feedback 2025-02-25 (DES-): prefer single preflight endpoint that aggregates checks but preserve per-check endpoints for operator UX.
Engineering update 2025-02-28: prototype preflight endpoints implemented behind feature flag; initial MTU probe uses TCP probe with varying payload sizes to detect fragmentation-induced latency.
Security review 2025-03-01: offline signing key process accepted with conditions — must record import events in audit logs and require operator-level approval for key replacement.
